ai.stableNodeKey: (outline) § subtitle#0

content.text: Opening a new database connection for the Ledger service incurs a cost of approximately 30 ms. This delay is due to the necessity of a TLS handshake and an authentication round trip for each new connection.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Why pool connections § text#0

content.text: A connection pool maintains a set of open connections, lending them to incoming requests. This mechanism allows most requests to bypass the overhead associated with establishing new connections, thereby reducing latency.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Why pool connections § text#1

content.text: The connection pool also serves as a protective measure by limiting the total number of connections the service can hold. This prevents the database from being overwhelmed during sudden traffic surges.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Why pool connections § text#2

content.text: Opening a new database connection costs 30 ms due to TLS handshake and authentication.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Why pool connections § text#3

content.text: Connection pooling avoids the 30 ms cost for most requests by reusing existing connections.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Why pool connections § text#4

content.text: The connection pool limits the number of open connections, safeguarding the database during traffic spikes.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Why pool connections § text#5

content.text: Each Ledger instance maintains a connection pool with a maximum of 20 connections.
The database supports a total of 400 connections, with 40 reserved for migrations and administrators.
This capacity allows for 18 Ledger instances at full size, leading to the autoscaler being capped at 18 instances.
Increasing the pool size is only beneficial when requests are waiting for a connection. If the database CPU is saturated, more connections will slow down queries.
A pool sized for peak traffic will hold idle connections overnight, consuming memory on the database but incurring no other costs.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Operating the pool § text#0

content.text: A request will wait a maximum of 2 seconds to borrow a connection before failing with a
POOL_EXHAUSTED
error.
The 2-second wait limit is intentionally shorter than the 5-second request deadline, allowing the caller sufficient time to return a clear error.
Each query has a statement timeout of
3s
, set using
SET statement_timeout = '3s'
when the connection is opened.
The statement timeout does not apply to migrations, which use reserved connections without a time limit.
Long transactions hold their connections for their entire duration, so the team aims to keep transactions under 500 ms.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Operating the pool § text#5

content.text: Before lending an idle connection (idle for over 60 seconds), the pool executes
SELECT 1
to verify its functionality.
If a connection fails the health check, it is closed and replaced with a new one for the request.
During a database failover, all open connections break. The pool is then drained and refilled from the new primary database.
Refilling is rate-limited to 5 new connections per second per instance. This prevents 18 instances reconnecting simultaneously from overloading the new primary.
Requests may experience
POOL_EXHAUSTED
errors for up to approximately 4 seconds until the pool is fully refilled.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Operating the pool § text#10

content.text: A connection borrowed for more than 10 seconds is logged as a potential leak, along with the stack trace of the borrowing code.
The pool does not forcibly reclaim leaked connections, as the code holding them might still be actively using them.
Most leaks identified by the team originated from error paths that returned prematurely without releasing the connection.
Leak warnings are reviewed weekly. Recurring leaks result in a ticket for the responsible team.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Operating the pool § text#15

content.text: The pool exposes three gauges: connections in use, idle connections, and requests waiting to borrow.
An alert is triggered, paging the on-call engineer, if requests have been waiting for more than 30 seconds consecutively.
A persistent queue typically indicates slow queries rather than an undersized pool. The runbook prioritizes investigating slow statements over adjusting pool size.
During a failover, the idle connection gauge drops to zero and recovers as the pool refills, providing a quick confirmation of failover completion.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Operating the pool § text#19

content.text: The Ledger connection pool is configured for optimal performance and resilience, balancing connection limits, timeouts, and health checks. It includes mechanisms for detecting and addressing connection leaks, and comprehensive monitoring to ensure operational stability.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Operating the pool § text#23

content.text: The system is designed with specific limits:
Max connections per instance:
Total database connections:
400 (40 reserved)
Autoscaler cap:
18 instances
Connection wait timeout:
2 seconds
Statement timeout:
3 seconds
Long transaction target:
under 500 ms
Connection leak detection:
10 seconds
Failover refill rate:
5 connections/sec/instance
Failover
POOL_EXHAUSTED
duration:
up to 4 seconds
Alert trigger for waiting requests:
30 seconds

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Operating the pool § text#24

content.text: During a database failover, the system gracefully handles the transition by draining and refilling the connection pool from the new primary. The refill process is rate-limited to prevent overloading the new primary, with a temporary period of
POOL_EXHAUSTED
errors expected. The idle connection gauge serves as a quick indicator of failover completion.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Operating the pool § text#25

content.text: The system actively monitors for connection leaks by logging connections held for over 10 seconds. While the pool doesn't forcibly reclaim these, leak warnings are reviewed weekly, and recurring issues are escalated to the owning team. This proactive approach helps maintain connection availability and system health.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Operating the pool § text#26

content.text: The pool exports key metrics (connections in use, idle, waiting requests). An alert is triggered if requests wait for more than 30 seconds, indicating a potential issue. The runbook prioritizes investigating slow queries over pool size adjustments in such scenarios, reflecting a focus on root cause analysis.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Operating the pool § text#27

content.text: A connection pool makes connections cheap and bounded.

ai.stableNodeKey: Running a shared connection pool › Takeaway § text#0

content.text: The pool's size, timeouts, and failover behavior must be configured in conjunction with the database's own limits.
